clue.text: Green turnover, the sweet of Napoleon's exile?

indicators.note: a turnover flips something over, so the pastry built from the next words is turned end to end

blocks.note: the Mediterranean island Napoleon was banished to in 1814
short for pudding, the British word for dessert

explanation.surface: A green pastry turnover offered as the dessert Napoleon ate in exile.
explanation.walkthrough: Turnover looks like the pastry itself but is the signal: ELBA PUD read backwards gives DUPABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means naive and inexperienced, so easily fooled or tricked by others.

clue.text: He composed for the lute in D: plus "The  _____ the Pussy Cat"

blocks.note: taken as written
Edward Lear's nonsense poem title, whose missing words fill the blank

explanation.surface: A lute composer's work listed in D, alongside a nursery poem title.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear's poem is 'The Owl and the Pussy-Cat', so the blank holds OWL AND; D plus that gives DOWLAND, the Elizabethan lutenist John Dowland.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dowland was the leading Elizabethan songwriter and lutenist, famous for his ayres and Lachrimae.

clue.text: One using a blind pig's trotter (I 'ad one fricasseed)

indicators.note: fricasseed meat is chopped and stewed, so the letters before it are cut up and recombined

blocks.note: taken as written
I 'ad taken as written, dropped aitch and all, then one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cockney cook boasting of a pig's trotter stew, served to someone blind.
explanation.walkthrough: A blind here is a deception or feint, not a person who cannot see, nor a window shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror relies on sleight of hand, feints and misdirection, which is exactly using a blind to deceive an audience.

clue.text: Spooner an admirer of Sandy Wilson was he?

definitions.text: an admirer of Sandy Wilson was he

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who spoons, old slang for kissing and cuddling a sweetheart

blocks.clueFragment: an admirer of Sandy Wilson was he
blocks.note: second meaning: the title of Sandy Wilson's 1953 musical comedy about a romantic admirer

explanation.walkthrough: Spooner suggests the reverend and his swapped sounds, but there is no spoonerism: to spoon is to court amorously. The Boy Friend is Sandy Wilson's 1920s-pastiche musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor who spoons with a girl is her sweetheart, and Sandy Wilson's best-known stage show bears that title.

clue.text: Caligula's horseplay?

blocks.note: first meaning: the Latin word a Roman emperor would use for a horse
second meaning: Peter Shaffer's 1973 stage drama about a boy who blinds horses
surface padding: the single word is split, its two halves serving the two meanings

explanation.walkthrough: Horseplay reads as one word for rough fun, but it splits into a horse in Caligula's Latin and a play; Caligula famously planned to make his horse a consul.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin noun for horse is also the title of Peter Shaffer's celebrated psychological drama for the stage.

clue.text: One getting the time from a record label

blocks.note: an extended-play record
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone learns the time from a record label, as if reading a clock off a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: Record label looks like one phrase for a music company; label alone is the definition and the record supplies EP at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive name or tag attached to a person, such as Ivan the Terrible.

clue.text: Spite re-engendered when one's discharge is thus prevented

definitions.note: a clause describing the condition, standing for the noun

indicators.note: something engendered afresh is produced anew, so the preceding word is remade in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
as in 'as he left', meaning when
I for one, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A spiteful mood revived at the moment a bodily discharge is blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine, epistasis is the checking or suppression of a bodily discharge or flow, such as bleeding.

clue.text: Hellenic horseman's heavenly humour

indicators.note: the possessive marks what the two words hold between them, so the answer is owned within their letters

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Greek rider whose mood or temper is sublime.
explanation.walkthrough: Humour here is the old sense of a bodily fluid, not wit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ichor is the ethereal fluid flowing in the veins of the gods, a celestial bodily humour.

clue.text: Like the Guardian's diarist, harpy had colonic disorder

indicators.note: a disorder is a muddle, so the letters of the words before it are thrown out of place

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist's tale of a shrewish woman with a bowel complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Disorder fits the medical surface, but here it scrambles the letters; the diarist is a columnist forever fretting about imagined ailments.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who constantly worries over imagined illnesses, as a fussy health-obsessed columnist might, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Lawrence Sikes's frail occupation

blocks.note: the initials of T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia
Bill Sikes's girlfriend in Oliver Twist; a frail is old slang for a woman

explanation.surface: A man called Lawrence Sikes holds a delicate job.
explanation.walkthrough: Frail looks like an adjective but is slang for a woman; Lawrence and Sikes are two different men.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenancy is the holding or occupying of property as a tenant, so the occupation of a house.

clue.text: Cricket's great hit created pain: so why was he run out? (See 14 down)

annotation.answer: WHEN YOU WISH UPON A STAR

blocks.clueFragment: Cricket's great hit created pain: so why was he run out?
blocks.note: surface reading: a big shot in a cricket match ends painfully and a batsman is run out

blocks.clueFragment: so why was he run out?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the reply to why a leading player got run out is that you wished pain on him; the Cricket is Jiminy Cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman's huge shot hurt somebody, and the question is why he was then run out.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is Jiminy Cricket of Disney's Pinocchio, whose famous song is the answer; to wish pain upon a star batsman is the joking reason he was run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Jiminy Cricket sings this Oscar-winning song in Disney's Pinocchio, making it the insect character's best-known hit.

clue.text: See 9
Petronius's book of the day: "I cry no tears"

indicators.note: to tear something is to rip it apart, so the three words before it are pulled to pieces and rearranged

blocks.note: the abbreviation for Saturday
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reviewer calls Petronius's work the book of the day yet says it moves nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: Tears looks like weeping, the noun, but it is the verb meaning rips.
explanation.definitionFit: The Satyricon is the comic Latin novel attributed to Petronius, Nero's arbiter of elegance.

clue.text: They are feeble with many more eccentric hesitations

definitions.note: a clause standing for the plural noun

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number
comparative of odd
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Frail old people who are even stranger and full of hesitant ums and ers.
explanation.walkthrough: Many more looks like a pair, but many alone gives D and more goes with eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodderers are weak, shaky people who totter about unsteadily, usually through age.

clue.text: Such purgatives use "Vacant" indicators

indicators.note: a joke on the clue itself: it uses vacant signals, so the letters before are rearranged with no real word telling you so

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Laxatives that empty you out, labelled like a lavatory door showing Vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: The vacant indicators are self-mocking: the clue admits its own signal is empty, yet the purgatives also leave you vacant.
explanation.definitionFit: Evacuants are medicines that empty the bowels, a class of laxatives or purges.

clue.text: Spokespersons, at day's end, are not like underwriters!

definitions.note: read as under-writers, people who write sparingly

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last of day is kept

blocks.note: PROs are public relations officers, who speak for a company
the final letter of day

explanation.surface: Company spokesmen at the close of business are nothing like insurance underwriters.
explanation.walkthrough: Underwriters are not insurers here but under-writers, writers who say too little; prosy writing is long-winded.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosy means tediously wordy and dull, the opposite of terse, sparing writing.

clue.text: Cricket's charge is constant: no blasted choice out East (See 9,10 across)

indicators.note: going out means leaving, so the compass point named after it is dropped from the word
something blasted is blown apart, so the following word is shattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: the mathematical constant
taken as written
taken as written
the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A cricketer's fee is fixed, with no wretched option in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is Jiminy Cricket, appointed Pinocchio's conscience; charge means the one in his care, not a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Disney film the Blue Fairy assigns Jiminy Cricket to look after the wooden puppet, his ward.

clue.text: Take one good mind set

blocks.note: R, from Latin recipe, is the abbreviation for take on prescriptions
the Roman numeral for one
the abbreviation for good
the id is the instinctive part of the mind in Freud

explanation.surface: An instruction to adopt a decent, settled way of thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Mind set reads as mindset; the definition is set alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Set in the sense of fixed or firm, as a jelly sets hard and stiff.

clue.text: Make a further modification to confit, as it were?

blocks.note: to con is to study or read over
fit meaning suitable
surface padding: the dish name is split into its two halves, which supply the pieces

explanation.surface: A cook alters a recipe for confit, the preserved duck dish, once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Confit is the French dish of meat preserved in fat, but it splits into con and fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To readapt is to adapt again, altering something once more for new circumstances.

clue.text: Compounds run in when in seed cultivation

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the running letter is placed within the word for when
cultivating ground turns it over, so the words before are dug up and reordered

blocks.note: as meaning when
the cricket scoring abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Chemical compounds seep in while seeds are being grown.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenides are chemical compounds of arsenic with a more electropositive element, such as gallium.

clue.text: Hot rod accessory? One might spare the rod

blocks.note: first meaning: an aerofoil fitted to a car to cut lift
second meaning: from the proverb spare the rod and spoil the child, someone who indulges

explanation.walkthrough: The two rods are unrelated: a souped-up car and a cane for punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail wing on a modified car is a spoiler, and an indulgent parent who never punishes spoils children.

clue.text: Characteristic trait disturbing, but ultimately docile

indicators.note: disturbing things moves them out of place, so the word before is jumbled
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the last letter of docile

explanation.surface: A personality quirk that is unsettling, though the person is gentle at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Characteristic trait looks like one phrase; trait is fodder and Characteristic alone is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a quality or feature regarded as belonging to someone or something.

clue.text: The feet of William Birkett

indicators.note: of here means made from, so the answer is formed out of the letters of the name

blocks.note: the end of the first name runs into the start of the surname

explanation.surface: A reference to the actual feet of a man named William Birkett.
explanation.walkthrough: Feet are metrical units in verse, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi is the plural of iambus, the poetic foot of one short syllable followed by a long.

clue.text: Get wind, say, of the "Solvers'' Guardian"

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the words are to be pronounced and the spelling follows the sound

blocks.note: a setter addressing solvers says your, and the newspaper calls itself us

explanation.surface: Catching a rumour of something to do with the newspaper's own solvers' pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Get wind sounds like learning a rumour; wind alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurus is the god of the east wind in Greek myth, and the name of that wind.

clue.text: Transport circuit in which one's invested capital

indicators.note: to invest is literally to clothe or surround, so the single letter is wrapped by the words around it

blocks.note: a car is a means of transport
a ring-shaped letter, like a circuit
the Roman numeral for one; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A transport loop that someone has put money into.
explanation.walkthrough: Invested and capital suggest finance; capital is a city and invested means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt, on the Nile.

clue.text: Committing no criminal act. Ah, to be a republican!

indicators.note: committing here means carrying out or perpetrating, so the letters that follow are acted upon and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sigh that opposing the monarchy is no crime, wishing to be a republican.
explanation.definitionFit: A republican opposes rule by a king or queen, preferring an elected head of state.

clue.text: Delays return of sewer rat we abandoned for one

indicators.note: something abandoned for another thing is dropped and replaced by it
a return goes back the way it came, so the whole thing is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Postponements in the comeback of a rodent we left behind in the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap WE in SEWERRAT for I to get SEIRRAT, then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or delay, so tarries means delays as a verb.

clue.text: Kitty's in Kent, right? Is one getting the wind up?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the kitty is placed within the abbreviation for Kent's region

blocks.note: Kent is a county in the South East of England
a kitty is a pool of shared money
the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cat living in Kent is getting scared.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting the wind up means getting frightened, but here it is literal: winding thread or tape up.
explanation.definitionFit: A spooler is a person or machine that winds thread, film or tape onto spools.
